subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After a deferred maintenance timeout releases the session lane, should later same-session maintenance be suppressed until the original worker settles, or may a new invocation run concurrently with that abandoned worker?
rationale: The public context-engine seam does not guarantee cancellation or re-entrancy for a still-running plugin `maintain()` call, so preserving liveness and preserving coalescing require an explicit owner decision rather than a local timeout tweak.

options.title: Decouple liveness from coalescing
options.body: Release the foreground barrier at timeout but retain a non-awaiting per-session record that suppresses replacement maintenance until the abandoned worker settles.

options.title: Allow concurrent replacement maintenance
options.body: Permit a later same-session maintenance call after timeout and explicitly accept the plugin re-entrancy and ordering risk as part of the context-engine contract.

options.title: Remove the new timeout path
options.body: Keep current coalescing by leaving deferred maintenance unbounded until a cancellable context-engine maintenance contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Decouple liveness from coalescing
recommendation.body: Release the foreground barrier at timeout but retain a non-awaiting per-session record that suppresses replacement maintenance until the abandoned worker settles.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the timeout and persistence-checkpoint implementation that needs the selected lifecycle policy applied.
